D.t: Gina Hinojosa trails by 2.0 and wins 32% of simulations. Closing it takes about 99,976 voters switching sides, or 199,953 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +7.7 and D +4.0. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +3.6. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +2.3; your worst is Marist University at R +6.1. 29 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Travis, a projected net 301,248 votes; Harris, a projected net 283,617 votes; Dallas, a projected net 269,122 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +5.8, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +1.9, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, R +2.6, 3.8% of the vote; Fort Bend, D +11.0, 3.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Gina Hinojosa runs furthest behind in Bell, Brazoria, Lubbock. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 57 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 52 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.10 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 37 to 61, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.06 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Gina Hinojosa: Immigration voters 22 to 77, Small counties 23 to 76, Midsize counties 33 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$4.0M cash against $18.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points toward Gina Hinojosa. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Cash: $18.2M in the bank against $4.0M for Gina Hinojosa.

R.t: Greg Abbott leads by 2.0 in the forecast and wins 68% of simulations. The cushion is about 199,953 votes; a one point swing is about 49,988 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.0 and R +7.7. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +3.6. Your best recent poll is Marist University at R +6.1; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +2.3. 29 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Montgomery, a projected net 91,747 votes; Parker, a projected net 45,593 votes; Smith, a projected net 37,309 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +5.8, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +1.9, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, R +2.6, 3.8% of the vote; Fort Bend, D +11.0, 3.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Greg Abbott runs furthest behind in Hidalgo, Cameron, Travis. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 42 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 47 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.10 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.06 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Greg Abbott: Black voters 20 to 79, Independents 27 to 70, Moderates 34 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18.2M cash against $4.0M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points away from Greg Abbott. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.

media.what: His 2WAY 'Midterm Blitz' coverage described both the Texas governor and Senate races as in play, citing Vance's return to the state and money flowing to Paxton.
Interviewed Democratic nominee Gina Hinojosa about what it would take to unseat Gov. Greg Abbott.

Interviewed Democratic governor nominee Gina Hinojosa on Face the Nation about four day school weeks, the uninsured rate, Greg Abbott's data center tax breaks and Elon Musk's donations to Abbott.
